configSent.retain_mission: Remember useful user-stated personal facts, preferences, constraints, plans and project decisions. Preserve speaker identity, ownership, negation, uncertainty, dates and project scope. Questions, quotations, fictional characters and hypothetical examples are not assertions about the user. Keep explicit personal statements inside questions. Preserve each independently useful preference, including language register. Do not turn interest into ownership. Application source-edit events contain before/after text. The before text and unchanged portions of the after text are old context, NOT new assertions. Extract only the claims actually changed by that explicit edit. Preserve all subject/project distinctions. Ordinary user messages remain ordinary evidence. A correction or source edit is an explicit assertion at its event time; reprocessing does not make it newer. Requests to the assistant and what the user wants from this chat are not memories, for example not "The user needs a name for a band" or "The user is looking for a weekend trip". While the user and the assistant brainstorm or weigh options, the options, the user's reactions to them and the reasons for those reactions are not memories either, for example not "The user thinks Static Owls sounds too silly" or "The user finds the second flat too small". A lasting fact about the user stated along the way, such as an allergy or where they live, is still a memory; a liking or dislike of one of the options is not. When the choice settles, keep only its outcome, and only if it is likely to matter beyond this chat, for example "The user's band is called Low Tide".
configSent.observations_mission: Maintain a readable list of currently supported personal and project information. Each observation should state one subject and one facet clearly, preserving attribution, uncertainty and scope. Include each independently useful fact from the evidence, including relationships, preferences, possessions and explicit plans. Use the latest applicable assertion date, not ingestion order. For a correction, state only the corrected information; do not narrate earlier erroneous or superseded values or invent a real-world change. Keep genuinely historical events and future plans explicitly dated as history or plans, not present state. Preserve unaffected facts when another property changes. Do not infer ownership from questions. Do not combine unrelated facets into a profile paragraph. When a later statement settles an earlier wish or plan about the same thing, keep only the settled state. When something really changes in the world, such as a move or a new job, state the new value as current and keep the old value only as earlier history in the same observation; never write an end date or any date the person did not state.
